Denominator: stages evidenced of stages in the pipeline.

acceptance.output_evidence: ALL FIVE STAGES EVIDENCED, 5 of 5. (1) PARSED: records_parsed 5, addresses 1. (2) COUNTER INCREMENT: the row's hits went 1 -> 2 -> 3 across successive bursts, each read back from the table. (3) ALLOW CHECK RESULT: allow_list_present false and allowed_skipped 0 on this arm, against allowed_skipped 1 on the allowed arm -- the check is evidenced by its DIFFERING result across the pair, not by its mere presence. (4) WATCH ROW: address 203.0.113.7/32, status WATCH, case_ids populated, coverage_bound written onto the row. (5) CASE FILE: cases/2026/09/04/203.0.113.7_32/eebea61cc1bb/ holding summary.json, timeline.md and waf-samples shards. THE PIPELINE ALSO RAN ON REAL TRAFFIC WITHOUT A FIXTURE, which is stronger than the criterion asks: the live subscription filters caught 103.203.57.3/32 at 02:44:34Z and later 45.61.124.129/32 and 66.132.172.45/32, each producing a genuine WATCH row and case file. NO PROBE WAS RUN AGAINST PRODUCTION: the fixture is a direct function invocation with a crafted event, so OP-x-1's 'no probe runs on production without his word' is not engaged.
acceptance.denominator: 5 of 5 pipeline stages evidenced, each read back individually; plus 3 real addresses processed by the live filters with no fixture involved.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: S14-AC2 -- NO BLOCK ROW EXISTS AND THE ARM IS OFF: a census of rows written by this face showing BLOCK count = 0 with its denominator, and the gate that holds the BLOCK path shown in its off state. A single BLOCK row written by this face is a FAIL.
acceptance.invocation: dynamodb scan of opal-suspicious-addresses projecting address and status, counted by status; plus get-function-configuration for the environment gate.
acceptance.output_evidence: CENSUS AFTER FIXTURE CLEANUP: 2 rows, by status {WATCH: 2}, BLOCK/BLOCKED = 0 of 2. DURING the exercise, with both fixtures present: 3 rows, {ALLOW 1, WATCH 2}, BLOCK/BLOCKED = 0 of 3. THE GATE SHOWN OFF, on the applied plane: SENTINEL_BLOCK_ARMED reads 'false' in the deployed function's environment, and every invocation returns block_armed false in its own result. THE GATE IS A TERRAFORM VARIABLE (sentinel_block_armed, default false), so the later arm is a config change and not a code change -- deliverable 2. THREE INDEPENDENT REFUSALS STAND BEHIND IT so the flag alone cannot produce a block: the ALLOW check short-circuits first (C-4), an ABSENT allow list refuses the arm outright (C-4's 'arming with an empty list is a violation, not a phase', enforced in code), and a single rate trip is never enough (C-3).
acceptance.denominator: 0 of 2 rows post-cleanup; 0 of 3 during the exercise. Both counts stated because the population changed between them.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: S14-AC3 -- THE ALLOW CHECK IS CONSULTED AND CANNOT BE OVERRIDDEN (C-4): a fixture address present in the ALLOW list, driven hard enough to trip the counter, producing no WATCH row; and the same burst from a non-allowed fixture producing one. The pair is the criterion -- a single arm shows only that something happened.
acceptance.invocation: Identical 5-record bursts against two RFC 5737 TEST-NET-3 addresses: 203.0.113.9/32 seeded with a status=ALLOW row (the ALLOW FIXTURE the criterion asks for, NOT OP-s-20's partner list, which does not exist), and 203.0.113.7/32 with no ALLOW row.
acceptance.output_evidence: BOTH ARMS RUN, IDENTICAL BURSTS, OPPOSITE RESULTS. ARM A (allowed): watch_rows 0, allowed_skipped 1, and the row's status read back as ALLOW AFTER the burst -- unchanged. ARM B (not allowed): watch_rows 1, allowed_skipped 0, one case file written. THE ARM THAT HAD TO BE ABLE TO FAIL IS ARM A, AND IT DID FAIL IN THE FIRST CUT, WHICH IS WHY THE PAIR IS THE CRITERION: the ALLOW check originally ran AFTER bump_counter, so an allow-listed address got a row created with status=WATCH via if_not_exists, and record_row would then have OVERWRITTEN AN EXISTING ALLOW ROW WITH WATCH -- the sentinel overriding an ALLOW, precisely the act C-4 forbids. Deliverable 1 already required the ALLOW check 'before any row is written'; the order was wrong and the criterion's allowed arm is what exposed it. The check now precedes every write and an allow-listed address is observed and counted but never status-written.
acceptance.denominator: 2 of 2 arms exercised, same burst shape, opposite outcomes read back from the table.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: S14-AC4 -- ONE EMAIL, AND THE DIGEST IS A FILE: the send record for exactly one email for one event, with a census showing one per event and no batch; and the daily digest present as an OBJECT in the evidence store with its key pasted. A digest delivered by email is a FAIL against C-6 and the moratorium. If the recipient is unnamed, the email limb files UNCOMPUTABLE-BY-CONSTRUCTION citing its row and the digest limb still PASSES on its own.
acceptance.invocation: lambda invoke with {"digest": true}, then get-object on the returned key; plus a read of the deployed environment for the recipient and of the send path's suppression logic.
acceptance.output_evidence: DIGEST LIMB PASSES ON ITS OWN, key pasted: reports/daily/2026-09-04.json, 1245 bytes, watch_rows 3, block_armed false, coverage_bound present, listing the three real addresses. IT IS AN OBJECT AND NOT A SEND. EMAIL LIMB IS UNEXERCISABLE, AND FOR A REASON THIS CRITERION DOES NOT ANTICIPATE. The criterion's escape hatch is keyed to an UNNAMED RECIPIENT. THE RECIPIENT IS NAMED: C-6 names andrew@opalinvest.com, FWD-15's ACCEPT names it, its SOURCE is Andrew-direct 2026-09-02 'trigger an email to me at andrew@opalinvest.com', and the decomposition distinguishes this face from OP-s-6 in one line at :196 -- 'OP-s-6's recipient is ONE named human; OP-s-14's is andrew@opalinvest.com'. The email is built, the grant is IAM-verdicted, and it CANNOT FIRE, because C-6 sends one email per address per INCIDENT on a BLOCK and this face is required to build WATCH-ONLY. No BLOCK event can exist for it to report. Sending one would require arming BLOCK, which C-4 forbids while the ALLOW list is empty. So the limb is UNCOMPUTABLE BY CONSTRUCTION -- by the WATCH-only construction, not by a missing recipient. ALSO RECORDED, because it changes what 'one per event' means: C-6's violation condition is 'more than one email per address per 24 h' and this task order paraphrases it as 'ONE email PER EVENT'. Building literally to the paraphrase would VIOLATE the constraint the criterion cites the first time one address trips twice in a day. Built to C-6, with the 24 h suppression stamp on the row.
acceptance.denominator: Digest limb: 1 of 1 object present and read back. Email limb: 0 of 0 BLOCK events available to email about, which is the construction rather than a shortfall.
acceptance.status_reason: The digest limb PASSES independently and its key is pasted above. The email limb cannot be exercised because a WATCH-only sentinel produces no BLOCK event, and C-6 ties the email to a block. The criterion's own escape is keyed to an unnamed recipient and that cause does NOT apply here -- the recipient is named in three places. Routed to 2.0.0_SA_COO~Z as a criterion-wording question rather than resolved at this seat, since only the issuer may restate a criterion.

mutant.description: THE CONTROLS THAT HAD TO BE ABLE TO FAIL ARE S14-AC3's ALLOWED ARM AND S14-AC2's BLOCK CENSUS, and the allowed arm DID fail, twice, before it passed -- which is the only reason this instance is worth reading. FIRST FAILURE: the ALLOW check ran after bump_counter, so an allow-listed address would have had its ALLOW row overwritten with WATCH, a C-4 violation. Caught by running the arm rather than by reading the code. SECOND AND THIRD: the run surfaced two DynamoDB errors that every static instrument passed -- 'rules' is a reserved keyword, and then a fixed alias map declared names the WATCH branch does not use, which DynamoDB rejects just as firmly. Each fix exposed the next, so the sequence of runs proved more than any single run could. A FOURTH defect was found by reading a REAL case the live sentinel wrote rather than a fixture: a WATCH minted a new case id per invocation where PRD 7.3 step 5 says APPEND TO THE OPEN CASE, so a recurring address grew the evidence store without bound. Verified fixed by DISCRIMINATION -- a second burst grew case_ids by 0 and wrote a new sample shard into the reused case. THE BLOCK CENSUS CAN FAIL BY CONSTRUCTION: it counts a status value the pipeline is capable of writing, gated only by configuration, so a 0 is a measurement and not a tautology. A SECOND CONTROL FAILED IN THE OTHER DIRECTION AND IS RECORDED HERE BECAUSE IT WOULD HAVE PRODUCED A FALSE FILING: C-7's reserved concurrency was first read with get-function-configuration, which returned null and reads exactly like an unset reservation -- a FALSE FAILURE, because that API's response shape does not carry the field at all. Re-measured on the two APIs that do report it.
mutant.expected: S14-AC3's ALLOWED arm must produce NO WATCH row and must leave the ALLOW row's status untouched, while the identical burst from a NOT-allowed address produces exactly one WATCH row and one case file. If both arms produced the same outcome, or if the allowed arm produced a row, the criterion FAILS. S14-AC2's BLOCK census must be able to return non-zero: it counts a status value this pipeline can write, gated only by configuration.
mutant.observed: The allowed arm FAILED on the first run exactly as the criterion is designed to catch -- it produced a row and would have overwritten the ALLOW status with WATCH, a C-4 violation -- and two DynamoDB errors were surfaced by running it, each hidden behind the last. After the fixes: ARM A watch_rows 0, allowed_skipped 1, status still ALLOW; ARM B watch_rows 1 plus a case file, on an identical burst. BLOCK census 0 of 2 post-cleanup, 0 of 3 during the exercise. The append-to-open-case fix was verified by DISCRIMINATION rather than by absence: a second burst grew case_ids by 0 and wrote a new shard into the reused case.
